claims.text: The trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation under POL-RD-01: the GPS polyline records 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km, an excess of 2.98 km or 36.34%, which clears both establishment gates — greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal. The finding rests on the trace figure, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing measurement, not the rounded actual_distance_km.

The route the rider booked carried no ERP at all. trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and the routing engine's stored optimal is 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. On the route the rider agreed to, the ERP line would have been zero, so the entire $4.00 of ERP on the bill is a cost the rider's own route never incurred.

Both gantry lines on the bill are CTE gantries the optimal route never uses — the fare breakdown itself marks each on_optimal_route false — and the trace passes the gantry points closely: nearest fix 0.0 m at 08:12:50 for the $3.00 CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry, and 40.2 m at 08:19:40 for the $1.00 CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry. The $4.00 of ERP is therefore the cost of gantries that only the detour, and not the rider's route, crossed.

Even taking the Braddell Road closure as a full exoneration of the detour under POL-RD-03 — as the rider in fact accepts — POL-RD-09(2) still requires off-route ERP to be refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, because the rider did not cause the closure either. The distance and time charges may stand; the $4.00 of CTE ERP does not.

The pass-through correction the rider seeks is $4.00 ($3.00 + $1.00), comfortably within the SGD 12.00 per-trip cap in POL-RD-09(2), so the whole ERP line is refundable and no part of it is barred by that cap.

The detour cannot be attributed to the rider, so POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund. The only message proposing the CTE was sent by the DRIVER at 08:12:30 ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah'); the rider's single reply 'ok' is a bare acknowledgement, not a rider instruction. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the rider-instruction test in POL-RD-04 cannot be met and the record contains no rider election to cross ERP gantries.

The trace is unbroken — 175 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07, the deviation finding rests on clean telemetry, and there is no gap-based basis for escalation under POL-RD-10(3).

claims.text: The rider clears the POL-RD-08 threshold limb on this trip's own trace — 11.18 km driven against a booked optimal of 8.2 km, an excess of 2.98 km or 36.34% — so the burden shifts to the driver, and the driver discharges it by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause: the LTA closure advisory ADV-20260714-031. No general assertion that 'traffic was bad' is made or needed.

POL-RD-03 exoneration is made out on all three limbs. (a) The advisory names Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — the arterial the platform's own optimal route uses, recorded as 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials' with optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00. (b) Its validity window of 05:30 to 12:00 overlaps the trip, which ran 08:07 to 08:36, with 35.2 minutes of overlap. (c) The actual route leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after, as the two CTE gantries crossed at 08:14 and 08:19 on a corridor the optimal route never uses show. The advisory text itself sanctions the CTE as one of the two lawful diversions.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap absorbs the whole excess: min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km. The justified excess equals the measured excess, so no residual excess survives on which a POL-RD-02 refund could be founded.

With the whole of the 2.98 km exonerated, POL-RD-02 has nothing left to run on and the driver's meter lines stand in full: base fare SGD 3.80, distance fare SGD 8.40 and time fare SGD 8.12. The rider was not billed for distance that was not driven — 11.2 km charged against 11.18 km on the trace — so no inflated or phantom distance line is concealed in the fare the rider challenges.

The single correction the policy requires — and the ceiling on the rider's recovery — is the off-route ERP. Under POL-RD-09(2) an external-event exoneration leaves distance and time standing but refunds the off-route gantry charges as a standalone pass-through: the two CTE gantries of SGD 3.00 and SGD 1.00, both recorded on_optimal_route false and both matched to the trace well inside the 250 m crossing test (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m). That is SGD 4.00, within the SGD 12.00 cap, and under POL-RD-09(1) it is never added on top of any POL-RD-02 figure. The contested SGD 9.00 is therefore not recoverable beyond SGD 4.00.

This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral attaches. The excess of 2.98 km (36.34%) sits below both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality lines, and the driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 553 — clear of both the 3-flag and the 0.05 ratio tests. No pattern may be built from any other, non-citable profile field.

The chat log independently corroborates the POL-RD-03 reason for the diversion and shows the driver's conduct was transparent, not opportunistic: at 08:12:30, before the first CTE gantry was crossed at 08:14:06, the driver told the rider 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah', and the rider replied 'ok' at 08:12:58. The diversion was driven by the documented closure, and the rider had contemporaneous notice of it.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute is decided on the trip's own trace and fare record, and both of you should read the reasoning the same way.

1. Was the route a deviation? Yes, on the measurement. The GPS polyline (EV-GPS-00103, 100% coverage, 175 fixes, no gaps, max gap 0 s) records 11.18 km against the booked optimal of 8.2 km (EV-TRIP-00103) — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34%. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (> 0.8 km and > 20%), and the trace figure governs over the rounded 11.2 km convenience copy. The excess is below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality lines, so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and POL-RD-06 is not engaged.

2. Is the deviation excused? Yes, entirely. LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) closes Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — precisely the arterial the platform's own optimal route uses ('Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials', optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Its window 05:30–12:00 overlaps the trip (08:07–08:36), the route leaves the corridor before the closed segment and rejoins after, and all three POL-RD-03 limbs are satisfied. The exoneration cap is min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, so the whole excess is justified. Because nothing remains after the adjustment, POL-RD-02 has no residual distance or time to refund: base fare 3.80, distance fare 8.40 and time fare 8.12 stand as charged, and no POL-RD-02 figure is added.

3. The ERP line, which is the part of this bill the rider is right about. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00103) charges two ERP gantries — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at 3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at 1.00 — and records on_optimal_route false for both, and the trace passes them at 0.0 m and 40.2 m respectively, well inside the 250 m crossing test (EV-GPS-00103). They are therefore real crossings of a corridor the rider's booked route never used. POL-RD-09(2) provides for exactly this situation: where the diversion is excused as an external event, distance and time charges stand because the driver is not at fault, but off-route ERP is refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, because the rider did not cause the closure either. That is 3.00 + 1.00 = 4.00, inside the 12.00 per-trip cap. POL-RD-09(1) does not double-count it, because there is no POL-RD-02 refund for it to be added on top of.

4. Points raised and answered. The driver's chat message at 08:12:30 ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah'), sent before the first gantry at 08:14:06, is contemporaneous notice of the diversion, not a rider instruction — the rider's 'ok' is a bare acknowledgement, waypoint_hint is null on both messages, and no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 exists, so POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP correction. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral is produced: the deviation is not MATERIAL and the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 553 completed trips in 90 days, clear of both pattern tests. No billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) arises either, because both gantry lines are matched to the trace rather than being phantom lines. Every artifact relied on here carries weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so no discount applies and none had to be disclosed.

Result: of the 9.00 contested, the distance and time elements stand and 4.00 of off-route ERP is returned to the rider. The charge is therefore partially refunded.

Both of you agree on the shape of this trip, and the evidence supports that agreement. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00103) records 11.18 km against the booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34% — which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal), so a route deviation is established. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) names Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — the arterial the platform's own optimal route ('Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials') traverses — its window (05:30–12:00) covers the trip, and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor before the closed segment and rejoining after. POL-RD-03 therefore exonerates the diversion: for the driver, the closure was real and the detour was driven because of it, not opportunistically (the driver told the rider at 08:12:30, before the first gantry at 08:14:06). The exoneration cap is min(2.98, 1.30 × (10.6 − 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, which absorbs the whole excess. No residual excess remains, so no distance or time refund runs under POL-RD-02 and the meter lines (base $3.80, distance $8.40, time $8.12) stand. That answers the driver's first four points in the driver's favour.

The one correction the policy requires is the ERP, and here the rider is right. The booked route carried no gantries at all (trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd = 0.00), and both CTE gantry lines on the bill — $3.00 at 08:14:06 and $1.00 at 08:19:41 — are marked on_optimal_route false and are matched by the trace within the 250 m crossing test (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m). Because the diversion is an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) leaves the distance and time charges standing but refunds the off-route ERP as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00; at $4.00 it is well inside the cap. POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the refund: the only message proposing the CTE came from the driver, the rider's 'ok' is a bare acknowledgement rather than an instruction, and with waypoint_hint null on both messages the rider-instruction test in POL-RD-04 cannot be met. Under POL-RD-09(1) this $4.00 is not added on top of any distance refund — it is the whole of the correction. The rider's request is therefore granted as to the ERP and refused as to anything beyond it.

No further money moves. The deviation is not material (2.98 km sits below both the 50%-of-optimal and the 8.0 km lines) and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 553 completed trips in 90 days, so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no driver-conduct referral arises. The trace is unbroken — 175 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and there is no gap-based escalation under POL-RD-10(3). Both gantry lines are matched to the trace, so there is no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4). The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the timestamps are consistent, so no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. All artifacts relied on carry weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. In short: the detour is excused, the distance and time fares stand, and $4.00 of off-route ERP is returned to the rider.

This ruling is addressed to both the rider and the driver.

WHAT HAPPENED. On 14 July 2026 the trip TRP-00103 ran from Blk 510 Bishan St 13 to Kallang Wave Mall. The booked optimal route was 8.2 km via Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials. The vehicle actually drove 11.18 km on the GPS trace (trip_record.actual_distance_km of 11.2 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and is not used for the threshold test). That is an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34% of optimal, which clears both establishment gates under POL-RD-01 (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). A route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own clean telemetry. Both advocates agree on this and so do I.

WHY THERE IS NO DISTANCE OR TIME REFUND. The LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) records an emergency water-main closure on Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — exactly the arterial the platform's optimal route traverses — active 05:30 to 12:00 on the trip date, with 35.2 minutes of overlap with a trip that ran 08:07 to 08:36. The actual route left that corridor before the closure and rejoined it after. POL-RD-03 is therefore made out on all three limbs. The exoneration is capped at min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, so the whole of the measured excess is exonerated and POL-RD-02 has no residual excess to run against. The base fare (SGD 3.80), distance fare (SGD 8.40) and time fare (SGD 8.12) stand, and the distance billed (11.2 km) matches the distance driven, so no inflated distance line is concealed in the fare.

WHY THE ERP IS REFUNDED. The two ERP lines on the bill are CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at SGD 3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at SGD 1.00. The fare breakdown itself marks each on_optimal_route false, and the trace passes each gantry well within the 250 m crossing test (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m). These are gantries only the diversion crossed. Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand because the driver is not at fault, but off-route ERP is still refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at SGD 12.00 per trip — the rider did not cause the closure either. The correction is SGD 4.00, within the cap. The rider's own booked route carried no ERP at all (trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00), which confirms the charge belongs to the diversion and not to the route the rider agreed to.

WHY POL-RD-09(3) DOES NOT BAR THE REFUND. The detour was not rider-caused. The only message proposing the CTE came from the driver at 08:12:30 ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah'); the rider's single reply 'ok' at 08:12:58 is a bare acknowledgement, not an instruction identifying a place or road as POL-RD-04 requires, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no rider election to cross ERP gantries exists.

MATERIALITY AND DRIVER CONDUCT. The excess of 2.98 km (36.34%) is below both materiality lines (50% and 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and no POL-RD-06 uplift arises. The driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 553, clear of both the 3-flag and 0.05-ratio pattern tests. No conduct referral is produced and no other profile field has been used for any finding (POL-GEN-01).

TRACE INTEGRITY AND ESCALATION. The trace is unbroken: 175 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero maximum gap, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and no escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. All trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and every charge line has a counterpart on the trace.

OUTCOME. The rider is refunded SGD 4.00, being the off-route ERP pass-through. The remainder of the contested amount is not recoverable: the distance and time charges stand for the reasons above. The amount contested is SGD 9.00; SGD 4.00 of it is returned and the balance is settled as charged.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you essentially agree on the facts, and the policy produces one narrow correction rather than a fight.

THE DIVERSION ITSELF IS EXCUSED. Your booked route (trip_record.optimal_route_source: 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry') runs through the stretch of Braddell Road that LTA closed 05:30–12:00 on 14 July 2026 for emergency water-main repair (EV-ADVIS-00103-01, ADV-20260714-031), whose window overlaps your 08:07–08:36 trip by 35.2 minutes. POL-RD-03 is made out on all three limbs, and its cap absorbs the whole measured excess: min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km. Nothing survives on which a POL-RD-02 distance/time recomputation could be founded, so the base, distance and time charges stand. The trace is clean — 175 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0 seconds — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and no gap-based escalation arises.

THE ERP IS NOT EXCUSED. Your route crossed no gantry at all (trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd = 0.00), and the two gantries billed — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00 — both sit on the CTE corridor the optimal route never uses. The fare breakdown itself records on_optimal_route false for both, and the trace passes within 0.0 m and 40.2 m of them (well inside the 250 m crossing test). POL-RD-09(2) says that where a deviation is excused as an external event the distance and time charges stand but the off-route ERP is refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip; the full $4.00 is within the cap. Because there is no POL-RD-02 figure, the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1) has nothing to subtract from — this $4.00 is the entire correction and is not layered on top of anything.

DRIVER: the diversion was justified on this trip, your chat message to the rider at 08:12:30 gave notice before the first gantry was crossed at 08:14:06, and no conduct issue attaches. The excess (36.34%) is below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality lines and your driver_profile shows 0 deviation flags over 553 completed 90-day trips, so there is no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral. Every gantry line is matched to the trace, so POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity does not fire and there is no phantom line. Your meter lines on distance and time are left untouched.

RIDER: the answer to your question is that you should not be paying for gantries you never chose to cross. You are refunded the full $4.00 of CTE ERP; the rest of the fare — including the extra distance the closure forced — stands. The rider's contention that the detour was not rider-requested is accepted: the only CTE proposal came from the driver, your 'ok' is a bare acknowledgement, and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund. The driver's contention that the diversion is fully excused under POL-RD-03 and that the ERP is the ceiling on recovery is also accepted.

RULING: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.00.
